## The examples

Three examples ship in both languages and are run by CI on every push; the outputs
below were recorded by running them, and the site build fails if the code shown here
differs from the files in the repository.

| example | what it covers |
|---|---|
| `penguins_workflow` | stratified split, recipe (impute, normalize, dummy), logistic regression, held-out metrics, 5-fold CV with the recipe re-prepped inside every fold, penalty tuning on a log grid, tune's selection rules, a JSON round trip of the fitted workflow |
| `ames_tuning` | an rpart-style decision tree on the Ames housing data over an explicit `cost_complexity` × `min_n` grid with repeated CV, `select_best`, the one-standard-error rule, `finalize` + `last_fit`, `fit_best` |
| `ames_workflow_sets` | two recipes × a linear model, a tuned tree and a boosted tree, mapped over one set of folds, ranked, and the winner refitted |

### Penguins: a classification workflow end to end

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

#### Rust

Run with `cargo run --release --example penguins_workflow` from the repository root.

{{< include generated/examples/penguins_workflow.rust.md >}}

{{< include generated/examples/penguins_workflow.rust.out.md >}}

#### Python

Run with `python examples/penguins_workflow.py` after `maturin develop --release`.

{{< include generated/examples/penguins_workflow.python.md >}}

{{< include generated/examples/penguins_workflow.python.out.md >}}

:::

The two outputs are formatted differently but carry the same numbers: the same
coefficients, the same cross-validated accuracy and log loss, the same best penalty.
Both examples pick the `linfa` engine explicitly to show engine selection; the default
engine is `native`, the port of R's own solvers.
